To avoid executing the same work item concurrenlty
currently busy workers according to their current work items and looks
up the the table when it wants to execute a new work item.  If there
already is a worker which is executing the new work item
is queued to the found worker so that it gets executed only after the
current execution finishes.
Unfortunately
column2: a work item may be freed while being executed and thus

column1: recycled for different purposes.  If it gets recycled for a different
work item and queued while the previous execution is still in
progress
column2: workqueue may make the new work item wait for the old one

column1: although the two aren't really related in any way.
In extreme cases
column2: this false dependency may lead to deadlock although

column1: it's extremely unlikely given that there aren't too many self-freeing
work item users and they usually don't wait for other work items.
To alleviate the problem
column2: record the current work function in each

column1: busy worker and match it together with the work item address in
find_worker_executing_work().  While this isn't complete
that unrelated work items don't interact with each other and in the
very unlikely case where a twisted wq user triggers it
onto itself making the culprit easy to spot.
